record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification results when varying BN parameters and its initialization, which bear on whether BN affects training performance. Its measured outcome is test accuracy over learning epochs, rather than the training-error measure in V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports separate CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 test-accuracy results for removing BN learnable parameters, and a CIFAR-100 test-accuracy comparison among zero-bias, random-bias, and BN initialization. It also reports CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 results from added noise to BN statistics. Figure 5's ImageNet and CIFAR-100 smart-initialization plots are figure-only and lack precise values; the text describes faster convergence and a higher-performing classifier. Cited findings about BN's speed and accuracy from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study explains BN geometry and tests frozen BN initialization, removal of BN affine parameters, and added BN noise. It does not compare training with versus without active BN for accuracy gains over time or learning-rate tolerance. Its initialization experiments also do not test V4's activation-matched signal/gradient preservation or plain-network depth claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that BN aligns spline partitions with data independently of gradient learning, providing useful initialization, and that mini-batch variation jitters decision boundaries and promotes larger margins and better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes BN geometry and tests BN initialization, fixed BN learnable parameters, and added noise to BN statistics; it does not reproduce a cited BN speed comparison using training-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: BN learnable parameters fixed or learned; BN-statistic noise variance; initialization choice (zero bias, random bias, or BN); dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing BN affine parameters changes final test accuracy: ImageNet accuracy decreases by 1.50–2.13 percentage points, while Table 1 shows changes ranging from a 4.8-point decrease to a 0.4-point increase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The contribution of learnable BN affine parameters to final test accuracy depends on architecture and dataset under fixed hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: BN-derived initialization yields faster test-accuracy gains and a higher-performing classifier when BN statistics remain frozen during SGD; Figure 5 reports a related ImageNet result.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-dependent initialization using BN statistics can accelerate accuracy gains without updating BN statistics during training.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing BN-statistic variances about 15% improves five-run average classification accuracy by 0.34 points on CIFAR10, 0.52 on CIFAR100 and 0.25 on SVHN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional noise in BN statistics can modestly improve classification generalization in the tested Resnet9 settings.

record.problems: The reported classification comparisons primarily measure test accuracy, not training error or the speed/tolerance measures in V6. Initialization curves are figure-only without exact values in the text. Appendix C Table 1 is flattened, lacks uncertainty, and shows inconsistent effects from removing BN learnable parameters; the authors say hyperparameter tuning may reduce some drops.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5's ImageNet smart-initialization accuracy-over-epochs results are described in text but the supplied figure has no dataset-readable numerical values, so they are not assigned a separate row. The paper also cites prior studies' BN performance results, which are not its own findings.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random labels, and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Teacher-student spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and prevention through identity shortcuts or the specified initialization alternatives.
Activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients, trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and very deep plain convolutional networks.
Loss, curvature, recovery and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Accuracy gains over time and higher learning-rate tolerance from active BN versus no BN; Fixup's speed and stability without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: V6 names accuracy gains over time, so test accuracy versus epoch is not inherently an unsuitable measure. R12 is excluded because the intervention is frozen initialization rather than active BN during training. Neither the initialization result nor the noise results justify the record's limits_scope labels. Figure 5 is already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, benchmark fitting, random or corrupted labels, network size, and early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error as depth changes; shortcut and normalization comparisons for training error.
Activation-matched initialization, gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature behavior around learning-rate stability thresholds.

Whether BN makes networks gain accuracy faster and tolerate higher learning rates in the specific systems named in the version; whether Fixup permits residual training without normalization; training error specifically.
